items.title: BlackRock's New Buffer Bitcoin ETF
points: BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF (PBIT) uses options (contracts giving the right to buy/sell an asset at a fixed price) on IBIT instead of holding Bitcoin directly, creating three overlapping tranches.
Each tranche typically limits initial losses to about 10% in exchange for capping gains, targeting conservative investors.
IBIT posted $665.2 million in net inflows Monday—its only inflow day among 12 U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs—reversing a two-week stretch that cost the funds $910 million combined.
Competitors like Calamos, First Trust, and Innovator already offer similar buffer products, but BlackRock's scale is expected to make a big splash.

items.title: Mt. Gox Repayment Delay
points: Mt. Gox trustee pushed the creditor repayment deadline to 2027 from the originally planned 2026, citing incomplete procedures from many former users.
$2.8 billion in Bitcoin remains to be distributed to creditors of the exchange that collapsed in 2014.

items.title: French Stablecoin Tax Legislation
points: French lawmakers passed an amendment by a single vote to tax swaps from crypto into euro or dollar stablecoins (cryptocurrencies pegged to a stable asset like the dollar) starting January 2027.
Gains are calculated coin by coin, meaning each stablecoin exchange is treated as a separate taxable event rather than aggregating all transactions.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation AI Security Warning
points: An Ethereum Foundation researcher warns AI could crack ECDSA signatures (the cryptographic math securing crypto transactions) before quantum computers become capable of doing so, urging industry action.

items.title: JPMorgan's Bitcoin Outlook vs. Recommendation Gap
points: JPMorgan's research team forecasts Bitcoin could deliver higher returns than traditional stock and bond portfolios over the next decade.
Despite the bullish long-term analysis, JPMorgan maintains it won't formally recommend Bitcoin to most clients.
Volatility and regulatory uncertainty are cited as the primary reasons for withholding a formal endorsement.
The stance reflects a broader institutional pattern: bullish research paired with conservative risk-management policies.

issues.subject: JPMorgan’s Bitcoin Forecast Comes With a Catch

headlines: JPMorgan projects Bitcoin could outperform stocks and bonds over the next decade, but maintains it won't formally recommend the asset to clients.
The bank's conflicting stance highlights the tension between institutional research showing Bitcoin's potential and conservative investment guidelines.
JPMorgan's forecast acknowledges Bitcoin's role as a diversification tool while citing volatility concerns and regulatory uncertainty as reasons for caution.

sections.title: JPMorgan's Bitcoin Outlook vs. Recommendation Gap
points: Research team forecasts Bitcoin could deliver higher returns than traditional stock and bond portfolios over 10 years.
Despite positive long-term analysis, JPMorgan maintains official position of not recommending Bitcoin to most clients.
Volatility and regulatory risks cited as primary obstacles to formal endorsement despite attractive return projections.
Pattern reflects broader institutional investor conflict: bullish research paired with conservative risk management policies.
